standard.title: Specification for Stranded Galvanized Steel Wire for Fencing (First Revision) (बाड़ लगाने के लिए गुंथे हुए जस्तीकृत इस्पात के तारों की विशिष्टि (पहला पुनरीक्षण))
standard.sector: Mechanical Engineering / Wire Ropes and Wire Products

sectional_committee.name: Wire Ropes and Wire Products Sectional Committee

standard.description: This Indian Standard specifies the material properties, plies, dimensional tolerances, galvanizing parameters, and testing protocols for stranded galvanized steel wire strands used primarily for fencing, agricultural enclosures, and security barriers.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard specifies the material properties, plies, dimensional tolerances, galvanizing parameters, and testing protocols for stranded galvanized steel wire strands used primarily for fencing, agricultural enclosures, and security barriers.

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to obtain a valid BIS license to stamp or attach the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' on wire bundles or packaging coils to demonstrate conformity.
requirements: Fencing strand is fabricated by twisting individual wires together, primarily in 3-ply (3-wire) or 7-ply (7-wire) configurations (comprising one core wire and six outer helical wires).
Standard individual wire nominal diameters range from 1.6 mm to 4.0 mm. A highly standard railway-grade and commercial specification uses a nominal single wire diameter of 1.6 mm.
Base steel must be drawn from low-carbon steel wire rods to facilitate cold drawing and tight helical twisting without physical joint failure or wire fracture.
Individual wires must undergo a hot-dip galvanizing process prior to stranding, conforming strictly to the medium or heavy coating requirements of IS 4826.
Wires must withstand wrapping around a mandrel of equal diameter for 8 complete turns without cracking, splitting, or showing zinc coating flaking.

Coating uniformity is verified using copper sulphate dip tests (conforming to IS 2633), requiring the wire to survive a minimum number of 1-minute dips without depositing bright, adherent metallic copper.
The lay length (pitch of helical turns) must be uniform to ensure balanced tension, using a standard right-hand ordinary lay unless otherwise agreed.
Observed or calculated dimensions, lay lengths, coating weights, and tensile strengths must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 to determine code compliance.
